Inis dom faoi Andrew Kerins.

Andrew Kerins (1840-1915), better known as Brother Walfrid, was an Irish Marist Brother who made significant contributions to education and football. Born in Ballymote, County Sligo, Ireland, he moved to Scotland as a young man during the famine years.

Key facts about Andrew Kerins:
- He joined the Marist Brothers religious order and took the name Brother Walfrid
- He founded Celtic Football Club in Glasgow in 1887 as a charitable venture to raise funds for the Poor Children's Dinner Tables, which provided meals to impoverished children in Glasgow's East End
- He worked extensively in education, teaching in schools in Glasgow
- He was deeply committed to helping the Irish immigrant community in Scotland
- He later moved to London where he continued his educational and religious work
- He died in 1915 in Dumfries, Scotland

His legacy lives on through Celtic FC, which has grown into one of the most successful and iconic football clubs in the world.
